sources.title: Jupyter Notebook format v4.5 JSON schema (nbformat)
sources.pin: branch main (floating ref at capture time); etag "5a268c8430e216c21dfbbe3301eef41af32e212c1b0d8c41a144c46b5012106f"
sources.locator: description "Jupyter Notebook v4.5 JSON schema."; definitions.cell_id pattern ^[a-zA-Z0-9-_]+$ minLength 1 maxLength 64; code_cell required [id, cell_type, metadata, source, outputs, execution_count]; execution_count: "Will be null if the cell has not been run."; output oneOf execute_result|display_data|stream|error; execute_result requires execution_count; error requires ename/evalue/traceback; nbformat_minor minimum 5
sources.establishes: Since minor revision 4.5 every cell carries a stable string id independent of position; code cells carry an execution_count (null if never run); saved outputs are structured and execute_result outputs bind to the execution_count that produced them; errors are first-class structured outputs.
sources.limits: Main-branch capture, not a release tag. A JSON schema validates document structure only; it establishes no runtime or execution semantics.

sources.pin: live API response at capture time
sources.locator: items[3] issue #88 "Nbclient waits indefinitely on killed subprocesses" created 2020-06-30T11:28:07Z, closed 2020-07-10T22:01:25Z, labels bug+help wanted, body: notebook subprocess killed by docker memory limit -> nbclient hangs forever, cites nbclient/client.py; items[0] PR #349 "Handle kernel dead status message in iopub polling" created 2026-06-15T11:50:06Z, state open, body: gateway broadcasts iopub status execution_state="dead", previously silently discarded because it does not match parent_msg_id; "This mirrors how _async_poll_kernel_alive handles kernel death detection"
sources.establishes: The failure (undetected kernel death hangs execution indefinitely) existed in nbclient as reported 2020; a kernel-death detection mechanism (_async_poll_kernel_alive) exists on main in 2026 per the open PR's description; a residual gap remains for remote/gateway kernels (PR #349 open, unmerged at capture).
sources.limits: Issue and PR bodies are claims by their authors, verified here only as recorded text; search snapshot is point-in-time; PR #349 not merged at capture.

sources.title: nbclient PR #90 diff (kernel-liveness fix + regression tests)
sources.locator: nbclient/client.py: new _async_poll_kernel_alive (loop: await asyncio.sleep(1); await self._async_check_alive(); on DeadKernelError cancel self.task_poll_for_reply); async_execute_cell wraps _async_poll_for_reply in task_poll_for_reply and on asyncio.CancelledError cancels task_poll_output_msg and raises DeadKernelError("Kernel died"); new fixture nbclient/tests/files/Autokill.ipynb whose single cell runs os.kill(os.getpid(), signal.SIGTERM); renamed test test_kernel_death -> test_kernel_death_after_timeout; new regression test test_kernel_death_during_execution ("Check that an error is raised when the kernel is_alive is false during a cell execution", pytest.raises(RuntimeError)); requirements.txt jupyter_client>=6.1.0 -> >=6.1.5
sources.establishes: The exact fix mechanism: a 1 Hz liveness poll task parallel to output polling, converting kernel death into DeadKernelError even when no cell timeout is configured; plus a regression test that kills the kernel mid-cell and asserts an error is raised.
sources.limits: A diff shows intent and tests, not release behavior. Merged status and date come from S4. Which release first shipped it is unresolved (lead L1); presence on main in 2026 is corroborated only via S3's PR #349 description.

sources.title: PyArrow 'Tabular Datasets' documentation source (apache/arrow main, docs v25.0.1 site)
sources.pin: branch main (floating ref at capture time); rendered site title 'Tabular Datasets — Apache Arrow v25.0.1' (separate capture e3bd1bf0ec25dd42e51123bde9c148f0583cb13d66957b4c9244003ed05ce6e1, superseded by this RST source)
sources.locator: "efficiently work with tabular, potentially larger than memory, and multi-file datasets"; "Creating a Dataset object does not begin reading the data itself."; schema inference "by default from the first file"; section "Iterative (out of core or streaming) reads": Dataset.to_batches returns an iterator of record batches, mean computed without loading full column; Scanner batch_size "default is one million rows"; ordering: "the order of the files controls the order of the data ... only applies when the dataset is constructed with a list of files. There are no order guarantees given when the files are instead discovered by scanning a directory"; section "A note on transactions & ACID guarantees": "no transaction support or any ACID guarantees", concurrent writes "may have unexpected behavior", "Most file formats have magic numbers which are written at the end ... a partial file write can safely be detected and discarded. The CSV file format does not have any such concept and a partially written CSV file may be detected as valid"; write_dataset max_open_files default 900, max_rows_per_file, basename_template overwrite warning
sources.establishes: A >RAM streaming scan mechanism (lazy dataset discovery + batch iterator); explicit non-guarantees that our data contract must paper over: discovered-scan order is unspecified; no ACID; partially written CSVs can be read as valid (crash-corruption risk); concurrent writers can clobber each other unless basename templates are unique.
sources.limits: Rolling main-branch docs (site shows v25.0.1); final ~2.7 KB not rendered (tail of write-section). Documents intended behavior, not measured performance.

sources.title: GitHub search results: duckdb store_rejects (issues #26211, #25825, #18980; PRs #26212, #26195, #26314, #26497)
sources.pin: live API response at capture time
sources.locator: #26211 (open, label 'reproduced'): with ICU loaded, CSV reader loads SQL NULL for unparsable TIMESTAMPTZ/TIMETZ "even with strict_mode = true and ignore_errors = false"; "ignore_errors = true keeps the row (as NULL) instead of skipping it, and store_rejects = true records nothing"; reproduced on v1.5.5 (d8cdaa33fd) and nightly v2.0.0-alpha (8cbdaba6ac); #26212 (open PR, fixes #26211): ICU casts "always returned true"; new test test/sql/copy/csv/test_csv_icu_tz_cast_error.test (require icu); existing tests csv_rejects_read.test and test_timestamptz_12926.test "pass in CI only because they run without ICU"; #25825 (open, 'reproduced'): read_csv with explicit buffer_size silently drops an oversized final row ("no error, no warning, and no entry in reject_errors"), row-count tables for 64KiB/1MiB/2MiB buffers; #26195 (open PR, fixes #25825): FinishBoundaryScan fix in string_value_scanner.cpp, test_buffer_size_final_row.test; #18980 (open, 'reproduced'): csv_line in reject_errors truncated near 10000 chars (v1.3.2); #26314 (open PR, Breaking Change label): "Currently, closing (or destroying) a result whose query hasn't finished: On autocommit: commits whatever the worker threads had already run"; "one path was and still is unprotected, which is the store_rejects path of read_csv"
sources.establishes: DuckDB has an explicit reject-capture facility (store_rejects option writing to a reject_errors table), and concrete live failure modes where ingestion silently produces wrong results (silent NULLing under ICU; silent row drop with explicit buffer_size; partial-write commit on closed results). All fixes were open/unmerged PRs at capture time on v1.5.5 / v2.0.0-alpha.
sources.limits: All items from one search snapshot; PR bodies authored by contributors; fixes not merged at capture, so release behavior is NOT established; remaining ~26 KB of JSON not rendered.
